appraisal_events.evidence: Swann grumbles that his wife 'n'a jamais pu savoir ce que c'est que l'heure' and, having become 'un peu ridicule' over having so inexact a wife who lingers at her dressmaker's, the narrator notes this 'inquiétait Swann pour son estomac, mais le flattait dans son amour-propre.'
appraisal_events.explanation: Odette's characteristically fashionable unpunctuality mildly irritates Swann and makes him faintly ridiculous, yet the narrator states plainly that it also flatters his self-regard, a small explicit sign that her behavior as a woman of the world continues to reflect well on him despite the surface annoyance.

status_effects.explanation: Despite genuine annoyance, Swann derives a private satisfaction of vanity from Odette's chronic lateness, a small local gain in his own self-regard that the narrator states outweighs the irritation.

ambiguities: Swann's reaction is genuinely double-edged (irritation and ridicule alongside flattered vanity); the passage does not make clear which note is meant to dominate, though the sentence structure places the flattery last.
